fields.title: Obesity
fields.bodyHtml:
Obesity: a comprehensive approach to treatment in Israel

Obesity is a serious condition that can lead to many accompanying illnesses, such as type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, cardiovascular disease and many others. Israel uses a comprehensive approach to treating obesity that includes not only changes to lifestyle and drug treatment but also advanced surgical techniques.

Diagnosis of obesity:

  1. Body mass index (BMI) measurement
    Helps establish the degree of obesity.
  2. Anthropometric measurements
    Assessment of waist circumference to establish the risk of developing accompanying conditions.
  3. Laboratory tests
    Blood tests for the lipid profile, glucose and insulin levels and other metabolic markers.
  4. Assessment of accompanying conditions
    Diagnosis of illnesses associated with obesity.

Treatment of obesity in Israel:

  1. Individualised diet and exercise programmes
    A diet and exercise plan adapted to each patient's needs.
  2. Drug treatment
    The use of medicines to correct metabolic disturbances and control appetite.
  3. Gastric banding
    A minimally invasive procedure in which a silicone band is placed around the upper part of the stomach, limiting the amount of food that can be eaten at one time.
  4. Gastric bypass
    Surgery in which part of the stomach and small intestine is bypassed, which reduces the absorption of food and promotes weight loss.
  5. Laparoscopic techniques using the da Vinci surgical robot
    The newest surgical techniques for treating obesity, which allow operations to be carried out with great precision and minimal intervention, considerably shortening the recovery period.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach
    Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of their particular medical and personal needs.
  • A multidisciplinary team of specialists
    Doctors, dietitians, psychologists and surgeons work together to offer the most effective treatment.
  • Access to advanced medical technology
    Including laparoscopic operations with the da Vinci surgical robot, which makes procedures less traumatic, allows rapid recovery and delivers excellent long-term results.
  • A comprehensive approach to treatment
    Not only weight loss but also improvement in general health, control of accompanying conditions and a better quality of life for patients.

Treatment of obesity in Israel aims to achieve a lasting result, including considerable weight loss, normalisation of metabolic markers and an improvement in patients' general wellbeing.

fields.title: Inguinal hernia
fields.bodyHtml:
Inguinal hernia: advanced treatment in Israel

An inguinal hernia is the protrusion of part of the internal organs through a weakened area in the groin. It is one of the most common types of hernia and requires surgery to prevent complications such as strangulation. Modern and effective treatments for inguinal hernia are available in Israel.

Diagnosis of an inguinal hernia:

  1. Clinical examination
    The doctor carries out a physical examination, during which the hernia may be detected when the patient coughs or strains.
  2. Ultrasound scan
    Helps confirm the presence of a hernia and assess its size and contents.
  3. Herniography
    A contrast X-ray examination, rarely used but possible for diagnosing complex cases.

Treatments for an inguinal hernia:

  1. Surgery:
    • Open hernia repair: The traditional method, involving an incision in the groin, returning the contents of the hernia and strengthening the hernia opening using the patient's own tissue or a synthetic mesh.
    • Laparoscopic hernia repair: A minimally invasive operation carried out through small punctures using special instruments and a video camera. It reduces pain after the operation and shortens the recovery period.
  2. Non-surgical measures:
    • Wearing a truss or hernia belt: A temporary measure that may be used before an operation or where surgery is not possible.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Highly qualified surgeons: Israeli surgeons have extensive experience in both traditional and laparoscopic operations.
  • The use of modern materials and technology: The use of high-quality synthetic meshes and minimally invasive techniques, which reduce the risk of recurrence and speed up recovery.
  • An individual approach to choosing the treatment: Surgery is planned taking account of the patient's individual circumstances, lifestyle and any accompanying conditions.
  • Comprehensive aftercare: Includes advice on rehabilitation, diet and physical activity to prevent the hernia recurring.

Treatment of an inguinal hernia in Israel aims at rapid recovery and at minimising the risk of future complications. Patients receive comprehensive medical support, from accurate diagnosis through to rehabilitation after the operation, which allows them to return to an active life confident of a successful outcome.

fields.title: Pancreatitis
fields.bodyHtml:
Pancreatitis: advanced treatment in Israel

Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas, which may take an acute or a chronic form and requires active medical intervention. Israel uses modern diagnostic and treatment approaches aimed at removing the causes of the condition, easing symptoms and preventing complications.

Diagnosis of pancreatitis:

  1. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood tests: Measurement of amylase and lipase levels, which may be raised in pancreatitis.
    • Full blood count (CBC) to assess the inflammatory process.
  2. Imaging:
    • Ultrasound scan: The initial investigation, to assess the structure of the pancreas.
    • Computed tomography (CT): A detailed image to assess the extent of the inflammation and identify possible complications.
    • Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP): Used to image the bile and pancreatic ducts.

Treatments for pancreatitis:

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Hydration: Intravenous fluids to maintain the balance of water and electrolytes.
    • Observation in hospital: To monitor the patient's condition and prevent complications.
    • Diet: A low-fat diet or temporary fasting to reduce the load on the pancreas.
    • Painkillers: To relieve pain.
  2. Endoscopic treatment:
    • Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP): May be used to clear obstructions in the pancreatic ducts, such as stones or strictures.
  3. Surgery:
    • Used in chronic pancreatitis to remove damaged areas of the pancreas, or for complications of acute pancreatitis such as abscesses or pseudocysts.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: A team of specialists including gastroenterologists, surgeons and intensive care doctors works together to provide a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Advanced medical equipment: World-leading technology and techniques that allow pancreatitis to be diagnosed accurately and treated effectively at any stage.
  • Individualised therapy: Treatment plans drawn up with each patient's individual circumstances, condition and needs in mind.
  • A high standard of patient care: All-round support for patients during and after treatment, including advice on diet and lifestyle to prevent further episodes.

Treatment of pancreatitis in Israel aims at a rapid improvement in patients' condition and at minimising the risk of long-term complications, which aids recovery and helps maintain quality of life.

fields.title: Squamous cell carcinoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Squamous cell carcinoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Squamous cell carcinoma is a type of cancer that develops from the flat cells of the epithelium and occurs frequently in the skin, the lungs, the head and neck, and the body and neck of the womb. Israel uses modern approaches to treating this condition, including advanced methods of diagnosis, surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy.

Diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma:

  1. Biopsy: The main diagnostic method, providing tumour tissue for histological examination.
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): Used to assess how far the cancer has spread and whether there are metastases.
  3. PET-CT: An effective method for establishing the activity of the cancer and its metabolic activity at an early stage.
  4. Laboratory tests: Blood tests to establish general health and organ function, and specific cancer markers.

Treatments for squamous cell carcinoma:

Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the body and neck of the womb:
  • Surgery: Radical hysterectomy with removal of the lymph nodes.
  • Radiotherapy and chemotherapy: Used in combination to destroy cancer cells and prevent recurrence.
Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the skin:
  • Local surgical removal: Excision of the tumour together with healthy tissue around it.
  • Mohs micrographic surgery: Precise removal of the cancer layer by layer, preserving as much healthy tissue as possible.
  • Cryotherapy and photodynamic therapy: For superficial forms of the cancer.
Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the lung:
  • Surgery: Lobectomy or pneumonectomy to remove part or all of the lung.
  • Chemotherapy and radiotherapy: For the treatment of local and metastatic cancer.
Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx:
  • Laryngectomy: Partial or complete removal of the larynx, depending on the stage of the disease.
  • Radiotherapy and chemotherapy: Often used as an alternative to surgery in order to preserve the voice.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, surgeons, radiologists and other specialists work together to develop individual treatment plans.
  • Innovative treatments: Access to the latest medical developments and technology, which allows the most effective and safest treatments to be used.
  • Highly qualified doctors: Israeli specialists are internationally recognised and have rich experience in treating various forms of cancer, including squamous cell carcinoma.

Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma in Israel aims to give patients the longest and best possible life, using a comprehensive and individualised approach.
